passages.text: Senseless people, become just judges of what is being said. For even if one ought to give oneself over to bodily enjoyment here, which feast is better: one by rivers and woods and groves, where there are banquets and drinking parties and shaded places, or one where there is the frenzy of demons, cutting of hands, cutting off of genitals, fits of fury and madness, clipping of hair, boasts, possession, shrieks, and all those things done theatrically to astound the senseless, so that you offer their owed prayers and thanksgivings to things deader even than the dead?

lexical_decisions.chosen: cutting of hands, cutting off of genitals
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves both named ritual injuries soberly without euphemism or added detail.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to things deader even than the dead
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the pointed comparative and its rhetorical excess.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὅπως τὰς αὐτῶν ὀφειλομένας εὐχὰς καὶ εὐχαριστίας καὶ νεκρῶν νεκροτέροις προσενέγκητε;
lexical_decisions.chosen: so that you offer their owed prayers and thanksgivings to things deader even than the dead?
lexical_decisions.rationale: Their preserves the printed third-person αὐτῶν alongside second-person you offer. It can refer to the previously mentioned senseless people, potentially including the audience. Your is a contextual identification alternative, but the main text does not silently harmonize the pronouns.

passages.text: And why do you do these things gladly? Since the serpent nesting within you, who sowed fruitless desire in you, does not want to tell you, I will remind you by explaining. It is like this: in the worship of God it is proclaimed that one must be clear-minded, exercise self-control, master anger, not appropriate what belongs to others, live justly, reasonably, steadily, and gently, and discipline oneself in deprivation rather than, when lacking something, take it unjustly from someone else and be filled. But among the so-called gods, the opposite happens. Some commands are also given to inspire awe at righteousness; yet even if you perform all the commands, ignorance of God alone is sufficient for your punishment. Nevertheless, you gather at the places you have assigned to them, gladly become drunk, and kindle altars. Their drifting sacrificial smoke, through the power, brings even the blind and deaf spirits to the place where they smell it. Thus, of those there, some are filled with possession, others with strange foods, while others turn to shameless conduct and others to thefts and murders. For the vapor of the blood there and the libation of wines set even the impure spirits themselves dancing. Lurking within you, they make you take pleasure in what goes on there, surround you through dreams with false visions, and punish you with countless afflictions. For under the pretext of the so-called sacrificial offerings you are filled with fierce demons, who also kill you while cunningly escaping your notice, so that you do not understand the plot against you. For under the pretext of some abuse, necessity, passion, anger, or grief, they remove you from life by hanging, by drowning you in water, by throwing you from a cliff, by your own hand, by a stroke, or by some other affliction.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ ἔνια εἰς κατάπληξιν δικαιοσύνης παραγγέλλεται
lexical_decisions.chosen: Some commands are also given to inspire awe at righteousness
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase relates certain commands to an impressive effect associated with righteousness. An impressive display of righteousness is another viable rendering; the main text does not decide that all such commands are merely fraudulent.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἡ κνίσα ῥεμβομένη καὶ τὰ τυφλὰ καὶ κωφὰ πνεύματα διὰ τῆς ἐξουσίας ἄγει εἰς τὸν τῆς ὀσφρήσεως αὐτῶν τόπον.
lexical_decisions.chosen: Their drifting sacrificial smoke, through the power, brings even the blind and deaf spirits to the place where they smell it.
lexical_decisions.rationale: Smoke is the grammatical subject, but the possessor or source of ἐξουσία is not stated. The power leaves it unspecified. Its power, assigning power to the smoke, is a defensible contextual alternative, not an explicit Greek possessive. No divine or demonic source of the power is independently added.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ αὐτὰ χοροῖ τὰ ἀκάθαρτα πνεύματα
lexical_decisions.chosen: set even the impure spirits themselves dancing
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the dancing image, not merely attraction.

lexical_decisions.chosen: by your own hand, by a stroke
lexical_decisions.rationale: By your own hand understands the demons as inducing the victims’ self-killing, supported by the listed pretexts and means of death. αὐτοχειρία can also be killing with one’s own hand, so direct killing by the demons themselves is a material alternative given the surrounding demonic subjects. Stroke preserves the separate ἀποπληξία without adding clinical detail.

passages.text: Therefore the prophet of truth, knowing that the world was greatly deceived and seeing that it had agreed with evil, did not love peace with it, since that peace arose from error. Setting out that it ultimately brings death upon all who agree with evil, in place of error he cast into those who had become clear-minded an anger against the one who had ambushed them, like fire and resembling a sword. Holding out the word, he does away with ignorance through knowledge, as though cutting and separating the living from the dead. So, as evil was overcome by knowledge in accordance with the law, war gripped everything. For the sake of salvation a son who yielded separated from a disobedient father, or a father from a child, or a mother from a daughter, or a daughter from a mother—in short, relatives from relatives and friends from companions.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὅτι εἰς τέλος ἐπιφέρει πᾶσιν τοῖς πρὸς κακίαν ὁμογνωμονοῦσιν παραθεὶς
lexical_decisions.chosen: Setting out that it ultimately brings death upon all who agree with evil
lexical_decisions.rationale: The object brought is implicit. Death is inferred from the end of 11.18 and the ensuing living/dead contrast. The it can be the peace founded on error or its sustaining error; no new punishment is specified.
The recipient of yielding is not explicit. The saving instruction is contextual, but the English does not insert that recipient.

source_issues.source_quote: ὅτι εἰς τέλος ἐπιφέρει πᾶσιν τοῖς πρὸς κακίαν ὁμογνωμονοῦσιν παραθεὶς
source_issues.issue: The object of brings upon is implicit. Death in the main text is inferred from the immediately preceding death-language and ensuing living/dead contrast. The antecedent can be error-based peace or its sustaining error.

The selected, image-checked edition prints a period between the article τῶν and noun νεκρῶν. English reads them together as from the dead despite this intervening punctuation. This is a supplied print feature, not assumed OCR corruption; no replacement Greek has been introduced.

passages.text: And let no one say, “How is this just, for parents to be separated from children and children from parents?” It is entirely just. For if by staying with them they not only did them no good but also perished with them, how is it not just for the one who wants to be saved to be separated from the one who does not want to be saved but wants to perish together? Moreover, those who had understood what is better did not themselves want to be separated, but to remain with them and benefit them by teaching better things. Therefore the disobedient, unwilling to listen to them, themselves fought against them, separating them, persecuting them, and hating them. But those who suffered these things pitied them as people ambushed by ignorance and, taught to understand, prayed for those who mistreated them, having learned that ignorance is the cause of sin. For the teacher himself, when nailed up, prayed to the Father that the sin of those killing him might be forgiven, saying, “Father, forgive them their sins, for they do not know what they are doing.” Becoming imitators of the teacher themselves, in their sufferings they prayed for those who inflicted them, as they had been taught. Thus they did not separate because they hated their parents, since they even offered prayers for those who were not their parents but had become enemies, and try to love them as they were commanded.

lexical_decisions.rationale: The dative connects instruction in understanding with the prayerful response, not with a newly supplied revelation.
Bracketed letters are already supplied by the selected edition; no new restoration has been made.
Follows the supplied bracketed reading and preserves the contrast with enemies.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀπὸ τοῦ μὴ θέλοντος, συναπολέσθαι δὲ βουλομένου;
lexical_decisions.chosen: from the one who does not want to be saved but wants to perish together?
lexical_decisions.rationale: The person described by βουλομένου remains the subject of co-perishing. To be saved repeats the contextual object of willing in the prior clause, not a new wish for other people’s destruction.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὅθεν οἱ ἀπειθεῖς ἐπακούειν αὐτῶν μὴ θέλοντες αὐτοὶ αὐτοὺς ἐπολέμουν, χωρίζοντες, διώκοντες, μισοῦντες.
lexical_decisions.chosen: themselves fought against them, separating them, persecuting them, and hating them.
lexical_decisions.rationale: The expressed αὐτούς is taken as the shared object of the parallel participles, giving the disobedient people agency in imposing separation. Separating from them is an intransitive alternative, but it is less source-transparent after the statement that the instructed people did not want separation.

passages.text: But tell me: how do you love your parents? If you do so with a constant regard for what is just, I join in your prayer; but if merely as it happens, I do not, for even on a small pretext you can become their enemies. If you love with knowledge, tell us what “parents” means. You will say, “Founders of a family line.” Why, then, have you not loved the origin of all things, if you have undertaken to do this with a just mind? But even now you will say, “We have not seen him.” Why, then, do you flatter insensible things without having searched? And what of this? Even if it was difficult for you to know what God is, you could not fail to know what is not God, so that you might reason that God is not wood, not stone, not bronze, or anything else made of perishable matter.

lexical_decisions.rationale: γένος links the argument to lineage and parentage. Origin or source here refers to God; progenitor of all is a viable more explicitly personal alternative.
Retains the prayer compound; join in wishing this is also possible, rather than bare agreement.
Preserves the separate rhetorical question introducing the final argument.
